_comment: wp_http.py retry policy — the one place a vendor or index API call is retried. NEVER a usage cap (project rule: no CTI-wide local caps; the vendor's own 402/429 is the limit): these values only bound how long ONE call keeps retrying a service that answered 'slow down' or dropped the connection. A timeout is never retried — the per-call ceiling (CTI_CALL_TIMEOUT) would turn that into hours. RULE 1: generic constants only.

retries._comment: How many times one call is retried after the first attempt, when the answer is a status in retry_statuses or the connection was reset / refused / closed by the peer. 0 disables retrying. A caller that needs a different count passes retries= for that call.

backoff_seconds._comment: Seconds to wait before retry 1, 2, … when the response carries no Retry-After header. The last entry is reused if a call is allowed more retries than the list is long.

retry_statuses._comment: HTTP statuses that mean 'try again shortly': 429 (rate limited) and the gateway failures 502 / 503 / 504. 500 is deliberately absent — it is usually a request the service cannot answer, and repeating it only spends quota. 402 is never retried: out of credits is the vendor's final answer.

retry_after_cap_seconds._comment: The longest a Retry-After header is obeyed for, in seconds. A longer value is waited for this long, then the call is retried; if the service still refuses, its status is returned to the caller as the vendor's answer.
